Accordion.notes: DOM: div.accordion[data-slot=accordion] > div.accordion__item (direct siblings; separator is ::after, absent on :last-child) > h3.accordion__heading (RAC Heading level 3) > button.accordion__trigger[type=button][slot=trigger][data-slot=accordion-trigger][id=T][aria-controls=P][aria-expanded=true|false]; then div.accordion__panel[id=P][role=group][aria-labelledby=T] > div.accordion__body > div.accordion__body-inner. React auto-adds the inner div (no part fn): Body className lands on the INNER div, other props on the outer. data-slot=accordion-trigger on the trigger is REQUIRED by CSS (accordion--surface rounds first/last item via [data-slot=accordion-trigger]). Indicator part (author places it, conventionally INSIDE the trigger after the label): with no children it renders the default svg.accordion__indicator[data-slot=accordion-indicator] 16x16 chevron-down (viewBox 0 0 16 16, fill none, aria-hidden=true, role=presentation, path fill=currentColor fill-rule=evenodd clip-rule=evenodd d="M2.97 5.47a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0L8 9.44l3.97-3.97a.75.75 0 1 1 1.06 1.06l-4.5 4.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06 0l-4.5-4.5a.75.75 0 0 1 0-1.06"); ml-auto size-4; a custom child element gets the class + data-slot + data-expanded via cloneElement. EXPANDED item: aria-expanded="true" on trigger (hover bg is suppressed by :not([aria-expanded=true])); data-expanded="true" on .accordion__indicator (rotates -180deg) and on .accordion__panel (REQUIRED: panel is opacity:0 without it); RAC also puts data-expanded="true" on .accordion__item (no CSS). Panel height = var(--disclosure-panel-height), set inline by RAC on the panel: "auto" when open, "0px" when closed, px only mid-animation; if unset, height is auto, so open panels need no inline style. COLLAPSED: hidden="until-found" + aria-hidden="true" + style="--disclosure-panel-height:0px" on panel, aria-expanded="false" on trigger. Disabled: disabled (or aria-disabled="true") on trigger. Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" on trigger (native rule is :focus-visible:not(:focus), never matches); hover works natively. Item gets data-hide-separator="true" (hides separator) when Root hideSeparator is set. Toggle/animation/single-vs-multiple expansion are RAC runtime.

propTargets.hideSeparator: Root (cascades to every Item via context; emitted as data-hide-separator="true" on .accordion__item)

hideSeparator.target: Item (attribute present with value "true" only when true; absent when false)

Accordion.openQuestions: partDetails lists no part for accordion__body-inner (auto-rendered inside Body).

Disclosure.notes: DOM: div.disclosure[data-slot=disclosure] (RAC adds data-expanded="true" when open; no CSS keys on it) > h3.disclosure__heading[data-slot=disclosure-heading] (RAC Heading level 3) > button.disclosure__trigger[type=button][slot=trigger][data-slot=disclosure-trigger][id=T][aria-controls=P][aria-expanded=true|false] (inline-block); then div.disclosure__content[data-slot=disclosure-content][id=P][role=group][aria-labelledby=T] (the panel; part 'Content') > div.disclosure__body[data-slot=disclosure-body] (p-2) > div.disclosure__body-inner (auto-added by React; no CSS rule; Body className lands on this inner div). Indicator part (author places it, conventionally inside the trigger after the label): with no children it renders svg.disclosure__indicator[data-slot=disclosure-indicator], the same 16x16 chevron-down svg as Accordion (ml-auto size-4, inherits color); a custom child gets class + data-slot + data-expanded via cloneElement; data-expanded="true" on it rotates -180deg. EXPANDED: data-expanded="true" on .disclosure__content is REQUIRED (opacity:0 otherwise), aria-expanded="true" on trigger; inline style="--disclosure-panel-height:auto" optional (var unset = auto). COLLAPSED: hidden="until-found", aria-hidden="true", style="--disclosure-panel-height:0px", aria-expanded="false". Disabled: disabled or aria-disabled="true" on trigger. Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" on trigger (native :focus-visible:not(:focus) never matches). CSS gap: no .disclosure__heading or .disclosure__body-inner rule exists (disclosure.css defines the flex heading rule as .accordion__heading by mistake), so the heading is a plain block. Toggling is RAC runtime.
Disclosure.openQuestions: disclosure.css/compiled CSS contains `.accordion__heading{display:flex}` instead of `.disclosure__heading`; treat .disclosure__heading and .disclosure__body-inner as classes without CSS rules.

DisclosureGroup.notes: Minimal static markup: div.disclosure-group[data-slot=disclosure-group] wrapping Disclosure blocks (div.disclosure ...). CSS only gives w-full and contain:layout style; no variants, parts or states. RAC DisclosureGroup (a plain div, no role) adds data-disabled when disabled (no CSS) and supplies expansion state to child Disclosures at runtime (expandedKeys, defaultExpandedKeys, allowsMultipleExpanded, isDisabled), so a static author sets each child's data-expanded/aria-expanded/panel markup by hand; only one child open is a runtime rule, not CSS. Accordion does not render this HeroUI component: it renders RAC DisclosureGroup directly with class .accordion.

Tabs.notes:
DOM: div.tabs[data-slot=tabs][data-orientation] > div.tabs__list-container (must be a DIRECT child of .tabs and parent of the list: secondary variant uses > .tabs__list-container > .tabs__list) > div.tabs__list[data-slot=tabs-list][role=tablist][aria-orientation][data-orientation] > div.tabs__tab[data-slot=tabs-tab][role=tab][id][aria-selected=true|false] (an if the tab has href); panels are siblings of the container: div.tabs__panel[data-slot=tabs-panel][role=tabpanel][id][aria-labelledby=] (tabindex=0 only when the panel has no focusable child). aria-controls= exists only on the selected tab. data-orientation="horizontal|vertical" (default horizontal) is REQUIRED on BOTH .tabs (flex-col vs flex-row) and .tabs__list (horizontal: w-full flex-row; vertical: flex-col gap-1 + separator geometry); React/RAC emits it on both. Dead CSS: .tabs__panel[data-orientation=...] margin rules exist but neither HeroUI nor RAC ever sets data-orientation on TabPanel, so they never apply in React (panel spacing comes from .tabs gap-2). SELECTED tab: data-selected="true" on .tabs__tab (+ aria-selected="true"), and the indicator is a child INSIDE that tab only:
(RAC SelectionIndicator/SharedElement renders a div only in the selected tab; absolute inset 0, z-index -1 behind the label because .tabs__tab is position:relative z-index:1; the sliding animation is runtime inline translate/width/height and is not reproducible statically). Separator: is a CHILD of a tab (absolute at left:0 / top:0); by CSS geometry put it in every tab except the first (inferred, React does not enforce). CSS hides it (opacity 0) when its tab or the immediately preceding sibling tab is data-selected, so tabs must be adjacent siblings; display:none in the secondary variant. Non-selected panels are not rendered by RAC: add hidden (or omit) on them (no CSS hides them). Disabled tab: aria-disabled="true" + data-disabled="true". Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" on .tabs__tab (native rule :focus-visible:not(:focus) never matches); hover works natively (data-hovered forces). Panel data-entering/data-exiting/data-inert are transient runtime states.

propTargets.orientation: Root (RAC emits data-orientation on Root and on List; TabPanel does not get it)

Tabs.openQuestions: Separator placement (child of each tab except first) is inferred from CSS (absolute left:0 inside the tab; hides when previous sibling tab selected), not from React source.

Table.notes: Block names differ: root is div.table-root (+ table-root--primary|secondary, data-slot=table); every part is table__* (there is no .table class). Use REAL table elements (CSS relies on th/td/tr/tbody tag selectors for corner rounding and column separators): div.table-root > div.table__scroll-container > table.table__content[role=grid][aria-label] > thead.table__header[role=rowgroup] > tr[role=row] > th.table__column[role=columnheader]; tbody.table__body[role=rowgroup] > tr.table__row[role=row] > td.table__cell[role=gridcell|rowheader]; optional div.table__footer as sibling AFTER the scroll container inside .table-root. Each part also carries data-slot=table-<part> (table-content, table-header, table-column, table-body, table-row, table-cell, table-footer, table-scroll-container); header tr has no class. Sortable column: th[data-allows-sorting="true"][aria-sort=ascending|descending|none]; its content is span.table__sortable-column-header[data-slot=table-sortable-column-header][data-direction] containing the label then an injected svg.table__sortable-column-indicator[data-slot=table-sortable-column-indicator][data-direction=ascending|descending] (16x16 chevron-up; only data-direction="descending" has CSS: rotate-180; rendered only when a sort direction is set). Row states on tr.table__row: data-selected="true" (selected cell bg; no native equivalent), data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true", data-dragging="true", data-drop-target="true"; hover/focus-visible work natively (data-hovered/data-focus-visible force). Tree rows: RAC sets inline style="--table-row-level:N" on each tr (1-based depth; also data-level=N, data-expanded="true", data-has-child-items="true") and the tree-column td gets data-tree-column="true" (padding-inline-start:calc(1rem*N)); no expand-chevron part is provided. Resizing: div.table__resizable-container (overflow auto) wraps the table; RAC then sets inline table-layout:fixed; width:min-content on the table and width on each th; th with .table__column-resizer loses its ::after separator; div.table__column-resizer is a runtime drag handle (RAC adds a hidden input). Load more: tr.table__load-more > td[colspan] > div.table__load-more-content. Virtualized div-based layout (role=presentation wrappers) is runtime only.
Table.openQuestions: partDetails.SortableColumnHeader.dataSlot shows table-sortable-column-indicator but the span carries table-sortable-column-header (indicator svg is a separate auto-rendered child with its own class, not a part). Nesting of ResizableContainer vs ScrollContainer is not enforced by React (unverified which wraps which in docs).

Pagination.notes: DOM: nav.pagination[data-slot=pagination][role=navigation][aria-label="pagination"] > optional div.pagination__summary[data-slot=pagination-summary] (first child) + ul.pagination__content[data-slot=pagination-content] > li.pagination__item[data-slot=pagination-item] > button.pagination__link[type=button][data-slot=pagination-link]. Ellipsis: span.pagination__ellipsis[aria-hidden=true][data-slot=pagination-ellipsis] with text content "\u2026" (typically inside an li.pagination__item). Current page: data-active="true" AND aria-current="page" on the .pagination__link (data-active has no native equivalent and drives the bg). Previous/Next: React HARDCODES an extra class, so the button is class="pagination__link pagination__link--nav" (data-slot=pagination-previous|pagination-next; no data-active) and contains an injected default (span has no class) followed by the label text; --nav gives w-auto gap-1.5 px-2.5. Disabled: disabled or aria-disabled="true" on the button. Size modifiers pagination--sm|--lg go on the nav only; links, ellipsis and summary are restyled by descendant selectors (no per-child modifier; pagination--md is inert). Hover/active/focus-visible work natively (data-hovered/data-pressed/data-focus-visible force). No page-number logic: the author lays out every page item.

propTargets.size: Root (nav); children react via descendant selectors, nothing cascades as a class

Pagination.openQuestions: Generator parts entry (Next/Previous -> pagination__link) is correct; pagination__link--nav is an additional literal class React always appends (see cssOnlyClasses), so no partFixes.

Breadcrumbs.notes: DOM: ol.breadcrumbs[data-slot=breadcrumbs][aria-label="Breadcrumbs"] (RAC default, en-US string, localized by RAC; it renders an <ol>, not a nav, so wrap it yourself if wanted) > li.breadcrumbs__item[data-slot=breadcrumbs-item]* , each containing a.link.breadcrumbs__link (React renders the HeroUI Link inside, so the anchor carries BOTH classes "link breadcrumbs__link") followed, for every item except the last, by the injected separator svg.breadcrumbs__separator[data-slot=breadcrumbs-separator][aria-hidden=true] (default 16x16 chevron-right svg, sized size-3, rotate-180 under rtl) as a SIBLING of the link inside the li. LAST (current) item: li gets data-current="true" and data-disabled="true"; its link is rendered as <span role="link" class="link breadcrumbs__link" aria-current="page" aria-disabled="true" data-current="true" data-disabled="true"> (a span, not an a) with NO separator. The CSS keys on data-current="true" on the LINK (text-link color, opacity 100; without it the aria-disabled rule from .link would dim it). Hover underline works natively (data-hovered forces). separator is a Root prop applied to every Item via context: a custom element separator gets class breadcrumbs__separator + data-slot added (cloneElement); a plain string/text separator gets no class. Part 'Item' is the li; Link and Separator are auto-rendered children, not separate parts.

propTargets.separator: Root (cascades to every Item via context; rendered as sibling of the link inside each non-last li)

Link.notes: Static markup: text. RAC renders only when href is set and enabled; otherwise (and aria-disabled="true" when disabled). HeroUI sets NO data-slot on the root. Optional icon after the text: . data-default-icon="true" is set ONLY when the default external-link svg is used (CSS adds ml-1 pb-1.5 to it); omit the attribute when you put your own icon inside link__icon (icon is size 0.75em, opacity 60, 100 on hover/press/focus). Disabled: aria-disabled="true". Focus ring only via data-focus-visible="true" (native rule is :focus-visible:not(:focus), never matches); hover/pressed work natively (data-hovered/data-pressed force). Combination .link.button drops gap and underline (link styled as button). RAC also emits data-current="true" when aria-current is set (no .link CSS for it; breadcrumbs use it).

Tag.notes: A Tag only exists inside a TagGroup, and size/variant are NOT Tag props: they come from TagGroup via context, so every static .tag must carry the cascaded modifiers itself. React always emits class="tag tag--<size> tag--<variant>" (defaults tag--md tag--default; surface -> tag--surface). DOM: div.tag[data-slot=tag][role=row] > (RAC wraps content in div[role=gridcell][style="display:contents"]) label text, optional svg icons (any svg inside .tag is forced to size-3) and the remove button. Selected: data-selected="true" (+ aria-selected="true") on .tag (accent-soft bg; no native equivalent). Disabled: data-disabled="true" or aria-disabled="true". Hover/focus-visible/active work natively (data-hovered, data-focus-visible, data-pressed force). Remove button is auto-injected when the group has onRemove (RAC then adds data-allows-removing="true" on the tag; no CSS): <button type="button" class="close-button close-button--default tag__remove-button" slot="remove" data-slot="tag-remove-button" aria-label="Remove tag"><svg data-slot="close-button-icon" 16x16 close x icon, aria-hidden/></button> (CloseButton contributes the close-button classes; .tag__remove-button only sets size-3 and color inherit). textValue is a11y only.

propTargets.size: TagGroup root (cascades to each Tag via context; becomes tag--sm|md|lg on .tag)
propTargets.variant: TagGroup root (cascades to each Tag via context; becomes tag--default|surface on .tag)

TagGroup.notes: DOM: div.tag-group[data-slot=tag-group] > optional label (shared Label: span.label[data-slot=label], not a tag-group part) + div.tag-group__list[data-slot=tag-group-list][role=grid, role=group when empty; data-empty="true" when no tags (no CSS)] > .tag items (see Tag) + optional description/error text. CSS adds p-1 to [slot=description], [data-slot=description], [slot=errorMessage], [data-slot=error-message] inside .tag-group; markup from the shared components: <span class="description" data-slot="description" slot="description"> and <span class="error-message" data-slot="error-message" slot="errorMessage">. size (sm|md|lg) and variant (default|surface) are TagGroup props that React puts on NO TagGroup element: they cascade via context to each Tag, where they become tag--<size>/tag--<variant>; the static author must put those classes on every .tag. Selection, removal and keyboard navigation are RAC runtime.

propTargets.size: Root (cascades to each Tag via context; emitted as tag--<size> class on .tag, nothing on TagGroup)
propTargets.variant: Root (cascades to each Tag via context; emitted as tag--<variant> class on .tag, nothing on TagGroup)

Chip.notes: Static markup: Text. React default classes: chip chip--default chip--secondary (chip--secondary has no CSS); size has no default, so no size class unless set (chip--md only repeats base text-xs; sm/lg change padding/text). Auto-wrap: if children is a plain string or number React wraps it in span.chip__label; any other children (icon + text, elements) are NOT wrapped, so wrap the text yourself. Icons: place svg directly inside .chip (no svg sizing rule exists, set width/height yourself). Chip is non-interactive: no state attributes, no hover/focus rules. Colors come from compound selectors: --primary has solid bg only for accent/success/warning/danger (chip--primary.chip--default has no compound rule and looks like secondary); --soft has compounds for all five colors; --tertiary makes bg transparent.

Badge.notes: Static markup: 3. React always emits a placement class (default badge--top-right), and every placement class is position:absolute with a +-25% translate, so a .badge must sit inside span.badge-anchor (position:relative; inline-flex; class hardcoded in React, no variants) as a sibling AFTER the host element, or inside another positioned ancestor. Omitting the placement class gives an in-flow inline badge (CSS allows it; React never produces it). Default emitted classes: badge badge--default badge--primary badge--top-right (badge--md and badge--secondary are inert no-op classes). Dot badge: leave .badge empty (min-h/min-w: 28px md, 32px lg, 16px sm). String/number children are auto-wrapped in span.badge__label; other children are not, wrap text manually. Ring around the badge is border: 1px solid var(--badge-border) (= var(--background)). No state attributes.

propTargets.placement: Root (.badge); the Anchor part takes no props

Avatar.notes: DOM: span.avatar[.avatar--sm|--lg][.avatar--soft] (Radix AvatarPrimitive.Root renders a span; HeroUI sets no data-slot on root or image) containing img.avatar__image[src][alt] and/or span.avatar__fallback.avatar__fallback--[data-slot=avatar-fallback] with initials/icon. No data-* or state attribute selects between image and fallback: Radix mounts the only after the image has loaded and renders the fallback only while it has NOT loaded (React never shows both). In static HTML include the one you want; if you include both, the absolutely positioned img (inset 0, size-full, aspect-square) covers the fallback once it loads, and a failed load shows the browser's broken-image box over it. The fallback ALWAYS carries a color class (React default avatar__fallback--default); color is read from Root (tv) and Fallback also accepts its own color override, but the class goes on the FALLBACK element, never on .avatar. variant=soft (avatar--soft on root) makes root bg transparent and gives the fallback a tinted bg per color class (avatar--soft .avatar__fallback--). avatar--lg also bumps fallback text to text-base via descendant selector; avatar--md is inert.

propTargets.color: Fallback (class avatar__fallback--<color>; set on Root it is forwarded to the fallback slot, Fallback accepts its own color override)

Card.notes: DOM: div.card.card--<variant>[data-slot=card] > div.card__header[data-slot=card-header] (flex-col wrapper for the title/description) > h3.card__title[data-slot=card-title] + p.card__description[data-slot=card-description]; div.card__content[data-slot=card-content] (flex-1 flex-col gap-1); div.card__footer[data-slot=card-footer] (flex-row items-center). All parts optional; layout is DOM order inside the flex-col gap-3 root. variant defaults to "default" in the component, so React always emits card--default when omitted (transparent = no bg/shadow). Card provides SurfaceContext {variant} to descendants unless variant is transparent, but no component in @heroui/react 3.2.1 reads it (grep-verified), so nothing to reproduce statically. No state attributes, no injected children.

Alert.notes: DOM: div.alert.alert--<status>[data-slot=alert-root] (React adds NO role/aria; add role="alert" yourself if wanted) > div.alert__indicator[data-slot=alert-indicator] > svg[data-slot=alert-default-icon], then div.alert__content[data-slot=alert-content] > p.alert__title[data-slot=alert-title] + span.alert__description[data-slot=alert-description]. The data-slot=alert-default-icon is on the svg, not the indicator div: CSS .alert__indicator [data-slot=alert-default-icon] sizes it to 16px content-box, so a custom icon needs that data-slot to get the same sizing. Injected default icon per status (all 16x16 viewBox, fill none, path fill=currentColor, aria-hidden=true, role=presentation; source icons.js): default -> InfoIcon (circle with i), accent -> InfoIcon, success -> SuccessIcon (circle with check), warning -> WarningIcon (triangle with !), danger -> DangerIcon (circle with !). Indicator/title color come from descendant selectors .alert--<status> .alert__indicator / .alert__title (no data attributes). status is a Root prop only (default "default"); no state attributes. Alert also provides SurfaceContext {variant:"default"} (unread, nothing to author).
Alert.openQuestions: generatorDraft.partDetails.Indicator.dataSlot is alert-default-icon, but the indicator div's own data-slot is alert-indicator; alert-default-icon belongs to the svg child.

Surface.notes:
Minimal static markup:
...
. React always adds surface--default when variant is omitted. Variants default|secondary|tertiary set bg plus the matching foreground token; transparent only sets bg transparent. Plain div, no parts, no state attributes. React also provides SurfaceContext {variant} to descendants, but nothing in @heroui/react 3.2.1 reads it (grep-verified), so there is no static counterpart.

Header.notes: Minimal static markup: <header class="header" data-slot="header">Label</header>. RAC Header renders a <header> element; HeroUI replaces its className with "header" (w-full px-2 pt-1.5 pb-1 text-left text-xs font-medium text-muted). It is a group/section label meant for RAC collection sections (ListBox/Menu/Select sections, e.g. a section wrapper with the header first) (static section markup unverified). No variants, parts or state attributes.
Header.openQuestions: Static section context for Header (how RAC ListBox/Menu sections wrap it) was not verified.

Kbd.notes: DOM: containing any mix of GLYPH (React Kbd.Abbr keyValue injects the glyph as text and the title) and K for plain key text. React sets NO data-slot on any Kbd part. Variant: tv defaults are empty, so no variant class is emitted by default (kbd--default is an inert class with no CSS); light adds kbd--light (transparent bg). keyValue -> glyph/title: command ⌘ Command, shift ⇧ Shift, ctrl ⌃ Control, option ⌥ Option, alt ⌥ Alt, win ⌘ Win, enter ↵ Enter, delete ⌫ Delete, escape ⎋ Escape, tab ⇥ Tab, capslock ⇪ Caps Lock, up ↑ Up, right → Right, down ↓ Down, left ← Left, pageup ⇞ Page Up, pagedown ⇟ Page Down, home ↖ Home, end ↘ End, help ? Help, space ␣ Space, fn Fn Fn. No states.
